name: Beth Mensah

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary day at your accounting firm look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The café sends me card receipts with tips mixed into the sales, and I separate them before preparing the accounts and tax schedule for a senior to review. I like finding the one refund that makes the till total right; I dislike explaining the same missing receipt to the owner on three different Fridays. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, and I am a junior still learning this job. I use AI now and then to suggest questions for the café owner, but I go back to the till slips before I enter a figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly plateaus, the café's tip slips still need sorting. The question draft helps a little, but I would still check the card total myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the senior what I checked and what the draft only suggested. I would tell the café owner to keep the refund slip with the day's takings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My pay is low for this job, and my partner Joseph and I have less than a month of expenses put away. Our grown daughter lives independently, but our remaining home-loan payment and Joseph's part-time community-centre wage make a missed week difficult; few accounting firms nearby would take me quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid café accounts and the current approved question draft, checking every number against the till slips. I would ask the lender for an exact remaining-loan schedule before changing our household budget, not assume retirement will wipe the payment away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the loan and our short reserve, although this version of AI does little harm. A small technology change does not make a missed wage small.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why check the loan schedule now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know exactly when the last payment is due. A written schedule would tell us whether a lower wage later could cover it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does your daughter help with money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown daughter has her own rent. I might ask her to explain a confusing letter, but I would not count her wages as ours.

say: I would show the senior **checked figures**, not just a suggested draft.
I would ask the café to keep **refund slips** with daily takings.
think: Our **low pay** and thin reserve make the home-loan payment worrying.
Few nearby accounting firms limit my **replacement work** if this post changes.
do: Keep **paid café accounts** and verify approved question drafts against till slips.
Request a **written loan schedule** before changing the household budget.
feel: I feel **anxious** about fixed payments and thin savings.
S0.quote: A small technology change does not make a missed wage small.
fieldNote: Her occasional AI use is a **question draft**, with figures checked against source slips rather than trusted from a fluent response.
She asks for a **loan schedule** because the current low wage and under-one-month reserve make fixed payments uncertain.

steps.text: Keep paid café accounts and verify approved drafts against till slips
Request written remaining-loan schedule before changing household budget

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI checks and writes more returns, the café file might need fewer paid junior hours. Robots would reach the physical counter later, but the screen work is mine now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to show us the wrong-tip examples before changing the review rota. I would say people should be trained on paid time if their jobs now require a new checker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own hours could realistically be cut, and Joseph's community-centre shifts do not cover our home loan alone. I have a little control if the firm gives a proper trial, but I cannot afford a long unpaid gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my supervisor Marta for a paid two-week comparison of anonymised café returns against signed originals, only with written approval. If the error count is acceptable, I would learn the approved AI checker on paid time and use it live only after written sign-off; if it fails or is refused, I would keep the paid manual checks while offered. If my hours fall in the first year, I would take a posted junior accounts role only with written wage, hours and start date that cover the loan and travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about possible cuts to my own shifts, but I can learn a tool that has been properly tested. I want to know which tips the AI checker mistook for sales.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the test count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Marta and I would count tip entries marked as sales and refunds missed by the checker. We would sign the result before a live file changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why insist on paid training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already earn little and do not want to lose a shift to a course the firm requires. A fair test uses the hours it saves, not my evenings.

I would ask for **paid training** on a required checker.
think: My own **junior hours** could shrink when AI checks faster.
Joseph's part-time wage cannot carry our **home loan** alone.
do: Compare **two weeks** of anonymised café returns against signed originals on paid time with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks.
Learn the **approved checker** on paid time after a signed pass; use live only with written sign-off.
After cuts take a **posted junior role** only with written loan- and travel-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost shifts.
S1.quote: I want to know which tips the AI checker mistook for sales.
fieldNote: She is willing to test AI, but **paid comparison** and written sign-off control live use.
A posted role needs **written terms** covering her loan and travel; a title alone cannot replace income.

steps.text: Test anonymised café returns against originals for two paid weeks with written approval; otherwise keep checks
Learn checker on paid time after signed pass; use live only with written sign-off
After cuts take posted junior job with written loan- and travel-covering wage hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could separate tips, check the return and answer the owner's questions faster than I can. Robots around 2031 would come later for the café counter; the accounts desk is at risk first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for a dated notice and severance plan. I would tell the café owner that a fast automated answer still needs someone accountable for a wrong tax figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to end my junior post once AGI takes the filing work. Joseph's wage will not cover the loan and basic bills, and our savings would last weeks; I wake up wondering how to avoid a missed payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would cancel the planned weekend coach trips and put their monthly saving into cash while my wages still arrive. I would keep every paid café file offered; if the post ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the small reserve for loan payments and food while seeking posted booking-clerk jobs, taking one only with written wage, hours and a start date covering the loan and travel. Booking is also thinking work, so I would treat an actual paid offer as a short bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect our main wage to go. I can forgo a trip, but a lender will still expect the payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask the lender for help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a payment looks likely to be missed after job loss, I would contact the lender before its due date about a temporary schedule. I cannot assume the loan vanishes because I am nearing retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a booking job last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I doubt it; AGI can take bookings too. I would accept a real paid opening as a bridge, not tell Joseph it solves everything.

say: I would request **dated notice and severance** before junior filing posts disappear.
I would keep a **named accountable person** for tax mistakes.
think: I expect my **junior accounting post** to end in 2028.
Our **weeks of savings** cannot replace my wage for long.
do: Cancel the **coach trips** and deposit the monthly saving while wages continue.
Keep **offered café files**; after loss use reserve for loan/food and contact the lender before a threatened missed payment.
Take a **posted booking job** only with written loan- and travel-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected job loss and the loan payment.
S2.quote: I can forgo a trip, but a lender will still expect the payment.
fieldNote: She expects **2028 desk displacement** before robots reach the café counter, and booking remains exposed thinking work.
The cancelled trips create **new cash saving** while wages arrive; the existing reserve funds bills only after a real loss.

steps.text: Cancel coach trips and deposit monthly saving while wages arrive
Keep paid café files while offered; after loss use reserve for loan and food
After loss take posted booking job with written loan- and travel-covering wage hours start
Contact lender before missed postloss payment to request temporary schedule

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me a chance to learn a small paid task before AGI reaches the tax desk in 2031. Robots around 2034 would be later for serving coffee, but they do not give my return extra time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to post a paid receivables-clerk vacancy before offering training. I would tell colleagues that a course fee should not come out of a household's emergency money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the routine filing work may disappear, but a supervised credit-control task could be within my reach. I am still learning and would need time to practise while my present wage continues.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one supervised overdue-invoice case each month only if Marta assigns it on paid time. I would read free receivables notes while keeping paid café files; if the firm posts a paid junior credit-control role, funds a short course fee and gives paid study hours, I would enrol. Before or after 2031, I would take the posted role only with written wage, hours and start date covering our home loan and travel; if filing work ends first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about lost filing hours, though five years gives me time to see whether I can do paid credit-control work. A practice case without paid hours will not pay the loan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Marta cannot assign a case?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the paid filing work still offered and use the free notes. I would not count a lunchtime lesson as a job path.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for a new role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Few similar firms are nearby, so I would read the actual travel hours and pay before accepting. The written wage after travel must still cover the loan.

I would protect **emergency cash** from speculative course fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years takes me to 68 when AGI reaches the accounting desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for café counter work, but I cannot assume I will still have filing hours by then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a written estimate of retirement income before announcing a date. I would tell Joseph and our grown daughter what the estimate actually says, not what I hope it says.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to stop working during that decade, yet I do not know if any retirement income available to me could cover the remaining home loan and food. Less than a month saved now means I need paid work until the numbers prove otherwise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a written retirement-income projection and the lender's remaining-loan schedule, then consider a date only if the projected income covers the actual loan, food and travel. I would keep paid café files while offered; if the post ends in the first year after 2036 while I still need wages, I would use the reserve for bills and take a posted clerk job only with written wage, hours and start date covering the loan and travel. I would not treat my age as an entitlement statement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the payments we have now, although the longer timetable lets me check them. A birthday does not tell the lender what I can afford.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the projection is not enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep working on the paid files the firm offers and apply for an actual posted clerk role if those end. I would not set a date that leaves the loan unpaid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Joseph retire too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Joseph would check his own figures separately. We cannot treat two unknown retirement incomes as one known household budget.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could take my junior wage before we know what retirement income would cover our loan. Dated notice, real posted work and paid training tied to a vacancy would help more than an inspiring speech.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether my partner's income will stay steady when I stop. I need our retirement-income and home-loan figures in writing before we choose a date.

headlineQuote: I need our retirement-income and home-loan figures in writing before we choose a date.
portrait: Beth is a **58-year-old junior accountant** with a bachelor's degree who is learning café returns.
Her **low pay**, under-one-month reserve, home loan and few local firms leave little room for error.
She uses AI **occasionally** for questions but checks each figure against till slips.
She will consider retirement only after **written figures** show income covers her remaining loan and essentials.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case could end her wage before retirement income is known.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **dated notice**, posted paid work and funded training tied to a real vacancy.
